topic: comparing models and making qualified data-based inferences
subtitle: Summarising a distribution, comparing two candidate models through their residuals, and saying exactly how far the resulting inference reaches

traps.desc: reported the median as the mean, which a right-skewed distribution makes visibly different
computed predicted minus observed, which flips the sign and reverses what the residual says about the model

problems.desc: Say which model fits better at that hour (the exponential one, whose residual is much smaller in size) and explain that one residual cannot choose a model: you need every residual, their sizes, and whether their signs show a pattern. Open explanation -- check the reasoning.

traps.desc: subtracted the smallest observation from the largest, reporting the range instead of the interquartile range
counted the two zero residuals as positive as well, so every hour looked like an under-prediction

problems.desc: Explain what the exponential model can and cannot support about a time far beyond the observed run: the fit inside the observed hours is evidence there, but extending it is extrapolation, growth of this kind is eventually limited by resources, and six observations from one run is a sample of one experiment. Open explanation -- check the reasoning.

Write a conclusion comparing the two models and stating a qualified inference: name the better-fitting model with residual evidence, note that its residuals are all non-negative so it under-predicts systematically, restrict the claim to the observed range, and say what a second run of the experiment would add. Open synthesis -- check the reasoning.
